How to order on LoloBuy without missing a step.

A practical workflow from the product link and specifications to payment and warehouse arrival.

⌕

Ordering workflow · 10 minute read

How to order on LoloBuy: a careful product-to-warehouse workflow

To order on LoloBuy without creating avoidable mistakes, treat the purchase as two connected stages. First, you select a marketplace product, confirm its specifications and pay for the item and any displayed cost to reach the warehouse. Later, after the item arrives and you review its warehouse information, you prepare and pay for an international parcel. The first checkout does not automatically include the final shipment to your home.

LoloBuy’s current web application supports product pages, a shopping cart, a manual-order form, an order-confirmation page, order payment and separate parcel submission. Its checkout labels distinguish the item total, freight to the warehouse, value-added service fees, discounts and the amount payable. The confirmation page also states that international freight is calculated separately. Understanding those labels is the foundation of a clean order.

1. Start with the exact product, not a screenshot

Use a current product link or a product already displayed in LoloBuy. A screenshot can help identify an item, but it does not preserve the seller, listing status, variants or current price. Before ordering, confirm that the page represents the seller and item you intended to choose.

Read the product title and description, then inspect the available specification combinations. A single listing may contain several colors, sizes, versions or bundle quantities. The cheapest displayed figure can belong to a different option from the one shown in the main image. Select the complete combination before treating any price as relevant.

The official product page explains that displayed pricing can be reference pricing and that the final transaction price is the one shown at order settlement. This matters when a seller changes a listing, applies a promotion or assigns different prices to different specifications. Work from your selected SKU and the checkout total, not an old social-media post.

2. Use manual ordering only when the listing cannot be handled normally

LoloBuy currently provides a manual-order page as well as the standard product flow. The manual form offers “Buy Now” and “Add to shopping cart” actions. It is useful when a valid product link cannot be converted into a complete product page, but it also requires more careful data entry.

For a manual order, copy the exact item link and enter only information supported by the seller’s listing. Record the product name, selected specification, unit price, quantity and any requested image in a consistent way. Do not guess a weight, material or variant that the seller does not state.

If the product information remains ambiguous, pause before payment. A purchase remark can communicate a specific request, but a remark cannot repair an unclear product identity. Ask for clarification rather than describing two possible choices and expecting the buyer to decide for you.

3. Lock the complete specification combination

Check color, size, model, quantity and bundle contents as one combination. For clothing, compare the seller’s measurement table with an item that fits you; familiar letter sizes do not guarantee identical measurements. For electronics or accessories, confirm model compatibility, plug or connector type and what the package includes.

Save a private record of the selected option before checkout. A short note such as “black, seller size L, one piece” is more useful than relying on the product thumbnail. If the listing uses translated specification names, compare the selected image and seller text as well as the translated label.

LoloBuy’s cart supports modifying specifications. If you notice an error there, edit it before submitting the order and confirm that the displayed image, property text, unit price and quantity all update. Do not assume that writing a contradictory remark will override the selected SKU.

4. Review the shopping cart by seller

The cart separates the item total from “Freight to warehouse.” This is domestic transport from the marketplace seller to the LoloBuy warehouse, not the later international parcel charge. A seller may apply its own domestic-shipping conditions, so review the displayed amount for the selected goods before continuing.

Check every cart line individually. Confirm the product image, specification, quantity, current unit price and seller. Remove duplicates created during comparison. If multiple items come from the same shop, the order-confirmation page groups goods by store and can display a store total and domestic freight.

Select only the items you are ready to purchase. Keeping a product in the cart does not freeze its availability or transaction price. Recheck any item that has been sitting in the cart, especially if its listing, seller stock or selected option may have changed.

5. Use the confirmation page as an audit

The current confirmation page asks for a sending country and provides an order remark for purchase requirements. It also shows product totals, domestic warehouse freight, value-added service fees and discounts where applicable. Read each section rather than jumping directly to the submit button.

The country selection does not turn the product order into an international parcel quotation. The official interface explicitly notes that international freight must be calculated separately. At this stage, you are confirming the purchase that should reach the warehouse; route selection and final parcel pricing come later.

Use the purchase remark for precise seller-facing instructions that match the listing, such as a stated color code or a request to avoid an unwanted substitution. Keep it short and testable. Do not use the remark to request undeclared goods, false customs information or a product the seller never offered.

6. Understand every part of the amount due

Before submitting, reconcile the total from the bottom up: selected quantity multiplied by the current unit price, any displayed item discount, freight to the warehouse, chosen value-added services and the final amount shown for the order. If the arithmetic or label is unclear, stop and investigate before paying.

Do not add an estimated international shipping figure from a blog or another buyer to this total and treat it as confirmed. International cost depends on the eventual parcel, destination and available route. The goods must first reach the warehouse so their recorded information can be used for parcel preparation.

Likewise, do not assume that a displayed service is automatically selected or free. Confirm which optional services appear in your own order and whether a quantity or fee is shown. The live confirmation page for your transaction is more reliable than a tutorial screenshot.

7. Submit once, then verify the order record

After the specifications and totals are correct, submit the order once. The application creates an order and routes the buyer to the order-payment stage. Preserve the order number privately because it connects later questions to the correct transaction.

On the payment page, confirm the order number, payment method, transaction currency, any displayed handling fee and total payable. If payment fails or remains under confirmation, return to the official order or bill record before trying again. Repeated clicks can make a simple failure harder to reconcile.

A successful payment should be followed by an order record and status. Do not create another copy of the order merely because a page was slow to update. Check the account’s order list and bill information first, then contact support with the private reference and exact status if the records conflict.

8. Track the purchase to warehouse arrival

After product payment, follow the order rather than an international tracking number that does not yet exist. The current account interface distinguishes pending payment, processing or purchase-related stages, shipment by the seller, pending receipt, arrival at the warehouse, completion and cancellation. The wording shown in your account is the relevant record.

Seller dispatch means the item is moving domestically toward the warehouse. It does not mean the international parcel has been submitted. When the goods arrive, inspect the item record and available photos against the specification you ordered. Raise a product-order issue while the evidence and seller transaction are still easy to identify.

Only after you decide which warehouse items to ship should you create the international parcel, choose available packaging or services, review the route information and confirm the parcel charge. Keeping these two stages separate prevents a common budgeting error: paying for the product and assuming home delivery is already covered.

A final LoloBuy ordering checklist

Before you click “Submit an order,” verify the product link, seller, complete specification, quantity, unit price, domestic warehouse freight, optional services, discount and order total. Confirm that any remark is specific and consistent with the selected SKU. Remember that international freight is a later parcel cost.

After submission, save the order reference, pay only through the official account flow and check that the status and bill record agree. Track the goods to warehouse arrival, review their recorded information and handle any mismatch before parcel submission. This disciplined sequence is slower than clicking through from a product image, but it gives you a clear record at every decision point.
